page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.126-1008 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 126 dedicated physical cores of the AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz, delivering 252 vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 1008.0 GB, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server type does not include bundled local storage or discrete graphics processing units, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

The AMD EPYC architecture integrates extensive instruction set support, including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and hardware cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. In benchmark testing, the instance scored in the top tier for both single-core (3440.78) and multi-core (428757.99) stress-ng execution. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registered at 525.28 GB/sec for read operations and 204.55 GB/sec for write operations. Compression and decompression workloads demonstrated sustained throughput, achieving 1644.5 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In-memory data handling reached 310.79 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside 169.89 GB/sec for static web serving. CPU-based language model prompt processing achieved 459.4 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

The absence of integrated NVMe storage represents a architectural tradeoff, directing I/O-intensive workloads toward configured network storage. While small model text generation scored in the middle tier at 178.03 tokens per second, large model text processing maintained top-tier comparative ranking for CPU-only infrastructure. The high density of physical cores combined with 1008.0 GB of memory makes the instance cost-efficient for heavy parallel processing without accelerator overhead. The server is suited for in-memory caching clusters, enterprise database instances, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.

Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic extensions. The high core density and uniform memory allocation deliver robust multi-threaded compute efficiency.
